findings.mechanism: Its genitive attachment under the second min makes fear a governed state in the security relation rather than an actor, direct object, or independent event.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the noun's grammatical position doing semantic work: fear is the state left behind.
findings.containment: This finding is the noun's contribution as a governed source-condition; it remains distinct from the preposition's own refrain and scope contribution.

epistemic.reason: The supplied noun attachment and source-condition analysis directly establish this word-level contribution.

findings.title: Indefinite fear stays open
findings.claim: The indefinite fear noun names a category of vulnerability rather than one specified enemy or alarm.
findings.mechanism: The genitive noun carries tanwin and no definite article, leaving the threat open while min still governs it as the source of relief.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can receive security as answering fear in its general human form, not only one historical danger.
findings.containment: The categorical openness does not activate every fear-related branch or specify an unnamed threat.

epistemic.reason: QAC morphology and the supplied category analysis directly support the claim.

findings.title: The ayah contracts vulnerability into a pair
findings.claim: The paired nouns contract the supplied movement from seasonal journeys and the protected House into bodily hunger and psychological fear.
findings.mechanism: The focus syntax preserves hunger and fear as parallel source-conditions, while the supplied 106:2 and 106:3 contacts connect them to the earlier scope of journey and civic security.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final divine care reaching both the body's deprivation and the mind's threatened horizon.
findings.containment: This is a local cross-ayah contact within the supplied pericope; it does not state a surah-wide thesis or rank the two vulnerabilities.

epistemic.reason: The critical contextual rows and local parallel syntax are supplied together.

findings.title: Attributed paired release
findings.claim: The paired causatives stage one collective moving from bodily lack and threat-expectation into nourishment and settled safety.
findings.mechanism: The feeding verb carries the food-giving act and is triggered by the hunger occurrence; the security verb carries settled safety and is triggered by fear. Their matching recipients and min-phrases make the two reversals mutually interpretive.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees food and security as two coordinated releases from coupled deficits rather than two unrelated benefits.
findings.containment: This is an attributed HFT reading anchored only in the supplied focus ayah. It does not replace the ordinary feeding-and-securing sense or claim that the two deficits are one condition.

epistemic.reason: All four trace coordinates agree with supplied focus occurrences, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound, so the synthesis remains attributed.
